_comment: klt erc supply spec for layout/utmi_stub.gds -- the T1 item 11
(power delivery, structural) supply-net read (#72). Item 11 is graded
from this run's supply findings, NOT from the report's overall `status`:
an antenna verdict or a floating-gate finding is a real defect but is
not this item's subject and does not block it (#1994).
Run it against the committed nominal-corner GDS:
klt erc layout/utmi_stub.gds layout/erc-supply-spec.json \
--top utmi_stub --pdk sky130 --format json
> layout/erc-supply-report.json
Pinned tool state -- load-bearing. The committed report MUST be
produced by a klt that actually implements stackup[0].active_layer
(klayout-tools#2001, poly n diff gate area) and the erc provenance
block (klayout-tools#1984/#2036, status + input/spec content hashes):
klayout-tools @ e8ca621a6961879cec1af60cc932c3b3d58ddcaa (upstream
main, an unreleased post-v0.5.0 state; the same state the run_digital
flow of gf180-drone-fc precedent used). The released klt v0.5.0 -- the
version this repo's flow records cite -- silently IGNORES
stackup[0].active_layer: its _validate_stackup reads
name/layer/label_layer/role only and passes unknown keys through with
no error and no warning, so the antenna denominator would be raw poly
area while the spec LOOKS like it requires poly n diff (verified by
A/B runs: gate areas 0.4-7.5 um2 raw-poly vs 0.1-2.3 um2 poly-n-diff
on the same layout). Reproducible invocation from a checkout of that
commit:
git -C <klayout-tools clone> worktree add --detach /tmp/klt e8ca621a
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/klt/src python3 -m klayout_tools.cli erc \
layout/utmi_stub.gds layout/erc-supply-spec.json \
--top utmi_stub --pdk sky130 --format json
> layout/erc-supply-report.json
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- `stackup[0]` MUST carry `role: "gate"` (klt erc's own contract), so
the stack starts at gate poly. `active_layer` (diff.drawing, 65/20)
makes the antenna denominator `poly n diff` instead of raw poly area,
which is what keeps tapvpwrvgnd_1 tapcell poly covers / filler-poly
out of `gates[]` entirely instead of reporting non-physical antenna
ratios for them (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md, 'Gate area: poly n
diff vs. raw poly area').
- li1 through met5 are the levels this block actually routes its
supplies on, ALL of them present in the merged GDS (klt layers:
full stack met1..met5 because item 11's digital column requires every
`power.straps[].layer` of the cited `klt place-and-route` run to be
covered by this spec's own stackup, and the committed P&R response
stages.place_and_route.power) straps met1, met4 and met5 -- three
layers spanning the whole stack, so a truncated stackup would break
the met4-to-met1 and met5-to-met4 connectivity and falsely split
VPWR/VGND into multiple islands.
- label_layer is declared only where the merged GDS actually carries
supply text: li1.label (67/5) and met1.label (68/5) carry the
standard cells' own VPWR/VGND rail/pin text, met5.label (72/5)
carries the PDN's own top-level supply pin text -- the sky130
equivalent of gf180-drone-fc's 34/10 + 81/10 pair in
layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json. met3.text (70/5) exists too
but is signal-I/O-pin-only (DataIn/DataOut), so declaring it would
add nothing; met2/met4 have no text datatypes drawn in this GDS at
all.
- GDS layer numbers are sky130's own drawn-layer numbers, resolved
from the PDK's own libs.tech/klayout/tech/sky130A.lyp (volare
open_pdks c6d73a35f524070e85faff4a6a9eef49553ebc2b) AND
cross-checked against klayout-tools' curated sky130 deck layer
table (src/klayout_tools/decks/sky130.py): diff.drawing 65/20,
poly.drawing 66/20, licon1.drawing 66/44, li1.drawing 67/20,
mcon.drawing 67/44, met1.drawing 68/20, via.drawing 68/44,
met2.drawing 69/20, via2.drawing 69/44, met3.drawing 70/20,
via3.drawing 70/44, met4.drawing 71/20, via4.drawing 71/44,
met5.drawing 72/20. They agree in every entry.
- vias[] bridges every declared stackup role in fabrication order --
licon1 poly-to-li1, mcon li1-to-met1, then the met1..met5 via
chain -- so the connectivity graph the supply islands resolve in is
exactly the wire/via stack OpenROUTE built. Note licon1 also
carries the standard cells' source/drain (diff-to-li1) contacts;
diff is not a declared conductor here, so those contacts join only
the li1 side of the graph -- the same registration shape
gf180-drone-fc's Contact (33/0, poly2-to-Metal1) uses.
- nets[]: VPWR and VGND, both `kind: "supply"`, matching the names
the cited `klt place-and-route` response itself reports
(`stages.place_and_route.power.power_net` / `.ground_net`) -- which
is what makes a short between them report as the severe
`erc.supply_short` rather than the general
`erc.multiply_driven_net`. Each must resolve to exactly ONE
electrical island: `erc.unconnected_net` fires on zero matches
(nothing in the layout carries that label at all) AND on more than
one (the rail is split into pieces that never touch) -- so ZERO
findings of that rule is exactly the 'one island per supply'
verdict, not merely an absence. The split-rail case is precisely
the no-PDN failure mode this spec exists to detect. VPB/VNB (the
well/bulk nets) are deliberately NOT declared: they label well
geometry (nwell.label 64/5, pwell.label 64/59) that is outside the
declared conductor stackup, so declaring them would only produce
zero-match `erc.unconnected_net` false findings; their story is
the well-tie half below.
- There is deliberately NO `ties[]` section here, and that is a
recorded gap rather than an oversight: on the installed klt 0.5.0
(the toolchain this repo grades with, per docs/characterization.md
provenance), declaring one on a real routed standard-cell layout
collapses the whole design into one electrical island and reports
a FALSE `erc.supply_short` (klayout-tools#2169, reproduced four
ways in gf180-drone-fc's FRICTION F-034; the fix has merged
upstream but is not in the installed klt yet, so T1's
toolchain-scoped rule says grade with what is installed).
Because `ties[]` is omitted, `erc.missing_tie` is NOT COMPUTED by
this run (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md: 'Omitted entirely ->
erc.missing_tie is never computed') -- its zero count in the
committed report is an absence of evidence, not evidence of
absence. The committed report itself says so mechanically: its
erc_coverage.inapplicable carries
`{"id": "erc.missing_tie:[]", "reason": "no_ties_declared"}` --
the not-computed marker, not a zero. What DOES stand in for it,
for this toolchain-smoke block, is: (1) the cited P&R response's
`power.pdn: true` with `power.tapcell_master:
"sky130_fd_sc_hd__tapvpwrvgnd_1"` -- real tapcells were placed
in every row (their instances are visible in the merged GDS as
`tapvpwrvgnd_1` on text.drawing 83/44, drawing taps on 65/44,
VPB/VNB well labels on 64/5 and 64/59); and (2) the same run's
independent, device-aware LVS report
`stages.lvs.power_connectivity.status: "match"` on power pins
including VGND, VPB and VPWR -- a netlist-compare check, hence
immune to klt erc's well-conductor modeling gap. Forward note:
the #2169 fix HAS landed upstream (klayout-tools#2186, included
in the pinned tool state above), so declaring `ties[]` -- and
upgrading this AC's missing_tie half from not-computed to a
checked zero -- is the natural follow-up once a klt release
newer than v0.5.0 becomes this fleet's installed baseline;
#72 pins this spec to the no-ties shape either way.
Layout/url provenance for re-verification: the committed report's
`provenance.input.content_hash` (sha256 of layout/utmi_stub.gds)
must match the committed GDS, and its `provenance.spec.content_hash`
must match this file.
